'''Purisimeño''' was one of the [[Chumashan languages]] traditionally spoken along the coastal areas of [[Southern California]] near [[Lompoc, California|Lompoc]]. It was also spoken at the [[La Purisima Mission]].<ref>{{Cite web
| title = Purisimeño
| work = Survey of California and Other Indian Languages
| access-date = 2012-07-22
| url = http://linguistics.berkeley.edu/~survey/languages/purisimeno.php
}}</ref>

A vocabulary of "La Purrissima or Kagimuswas (Purismeno Chumash)" was collected by [[Henry Wetherbee Henshaw]] in 1884.<ref>{{Cite web
| last = Henshaw
| first = Henry Wetherbee
| title = Santa Barbara (Barbareno Chumash) and La Purrissima or Kagimuswas (Purismeno Chumash) vocabularies September 18, 1884
| access-date = 2013-05-08
| url = http://siris-archives.si.edu/ipac20/ipac.jsp?uri=full=3100001~!16001!0
}}</ref> [[John P. Harrington]] also documented the language, and wrote a sketch of the grammar.<ref>{{Cite web
| title = Papers of John P. Harrington, Part 3, Southern California Basin
| work = California Language Archive
| access-date = 2013-05-08
| url = http://cla.berkeley.edu/item/1234
}}</ref>

Dr. Timothy Henry of the [[Western Institute for Endangered Language Documentation]] (WIELD) created a dictionary of the language.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wieldoc.org/?page_id=316|title = Purisimeño Project}}</ref>

=== Articles ===
Like many Chumashan languages, Purisimeño contains [[Article (grammar)|articles]] which can and possibly must be used in combination with [[Noun|nouns]]. Their exact function is unclear but some inferences can be gained. The first article, the [[prefix]] {{lang|puy|’a-}} seemingly was used a default in citation form and can tentatively be interpreted as a [[Marker (linguistics)|marker]] of indefiniteness or unidentifiability, while the second article, the prefix {{lang|puy|ka-}} can in turn be interpreted as a marker of [[definiteness]] and/or identifiability. Though, due to a lack of surviving sources on the language it is difficult to say this with certainty.<ref name=":0" />

=== Associative case ===
The [[associative case]] in Purisimeño is marked by the prefixes {{lang|puy|itš-}}, {{lang|puy|is-}}, {{lang|puy|iš-}}, or {{lang|puy|its̓-}}; and is used with nouns that usually have a strong association with a particular person such as the words for friend ({{lang|puy|'''itš'''antǝk}}), carrying net ({{lang|puy|'''iš'''tiwa’a}}), [[Little finger|pinkie]] ({{lang|puy|'''iš'''watimitš’i}}), and [[thumb]] ({{lang|puy|'''iš'''watinox̂}}).<ref name=":0" />

=== Tense ===
Purisimeño had three tense markers for [[Future tense|future]], immediate future, and [[past tense]] with the past tense {{lang|puy|-waš}} being attested in nouns which had some relation to the past but where somehow still relevant in the present such as footprint ({{lang|puy|’e’ewaš}}).<ref name=":0" />
